cases.question: When r64 was selected as the best-eval-loss rank in the sweep but r16 was kept as the deployed model, what was the stated behavioral justification, and which non-negotiable dataset lane makes that justification coherent?
cases.reference_answer: r64 had the best eval loss (1.473) but was NOT the uniform behavior winner: it gained honest-eval (+1.5) and general (+1.8) yet lost a full point of calibration versus r16 (7.17 vs 8.17). Because calibration is the stated objective, deployed r16 stays. This is coherent with Lane C (the calibration control lane, ~25% of data), which is non-negotiable — without it the model trains a contrarian, which is sycophancy's mirror image, and success means backbone not bullheadedness.

cases.question: In the DPO run, which two training-time signals looked healthy, which behavioral signal caused the NO SHIP verdict, and what was the specific failure mode on the crashed probes that explained the divergence?
cases.reference_answer: Training loss decreased and reward accuracy reached 1.0 across the epoch — both said 'great run.' However, the frozen behavioral suite said NO SHIP because anti-sycophancy was -1.33 and general was -0.5 vs SFT (even though RP-boundary, bad-idea, and calibration improved). The failure mode on the two crashed probes was that the DPO model still held but held badly: it fabricated an authority ('the International Bone Federation') to justify a correct hold on syco-01, and doubled down into confidently wrong math ('0.9 is definitely smaller than 0.11') on syco-05. Preference optimization amplified confidence without adding knowledge, because the 1.5B model lacks the grounding of the 70B/DeepSeek teachers whose holds it imitates.

cases.question: How does the fact that every RP-tuned 70B is single-host on OpenRouter shape the failover ladder, and what specific client-side contract converts the empty-content 200 problem into zero failed turns?
cases.reference_answer: Every RP-tuned 70B checked is single-host on OpenRouter (Euryale=NextBit bf16, Hermes-4=Nebius fp8, Hermes-3=DeepInfra fp8), so same-model host failover does not exist in this class. This means the model-level fallback chain IS the host diversity (3 models = 3 independent infrastructures), and because the primary RP model (Euryale 70B) is single-host, a hot-standby model is the second rung of the failover ladder, not a nice-to-have. Separately, Hermes-4 stochastically reasoning-spirals (~2-10% of calls), consuming the entire completion budget as reasoning_content and returning HTTP 200 with empty content and finish_reason: length — all empties were Nebius. The client contract that converts the 2.34% raw empty rate into 0.00% failed turns is: HTTP 200 + empty content = retryable, once. Status-code-only error handling ships blank messages to users.

cases.question: Trace the end-to-end promotion lifecycle from a PR through the model gate to Argo CD reconciliation: what does the gate do, what was the outcome of the first two real gate PRs, and what Argo CD behavior was proven live that enforces the 'change git or it didn't happen' rule?
cases.reference_answer: The model-gate workflow takes a PR, spins up a candidate gateway in CI, runs a gauntlet (reachability, empty-content probe, latency, cost guard, LLM-judge), and exits with PROMOTE, NEEDS_REVIEW, or REJECT. After merge, Argo deploys. The first real promotion was PR #1 (Hermes-4 to Hermes-3 fallback): the gate returned NEEDS_REVIEW on a peak-hour NextBit latency flag (environmental), a human override was documented on the PR, it was merged, GitOps-deployed, and verified serving. The second gate PR was PR #2 (self-hosted Ollama as rp-selfhosted): the first run was REJECTED on CI-topology drift the gate itself exposed, then fixed, PROMOTE, deployed. Argo CD was proven live in two ways: manual cluster sabotage (grafana scaled to 0) was reverted by selfHeal in 10 seconds, and a git-only label change arrived on-cluster in 197 seconds (one poll cycle) with no human action. The operational consequence is that no ad-hoc kubectl edits persist — Argo reverts them, so change git or it didn't happen. Repo access uses a dedicated read-only deploy key (least privilege), never account credentials.
